title: in/at/on (position) 1
subtitle: in the room / at the door / on the wall
summary: Use in for something inside a space, at for a point or place, and on for a surface.

lesson.heading: in = inside a space
lesson.text: We use **in** when something is inside a larger space: in a room, in a building, in a box, in a garden, in a town, in the city centre, in a pool, in the sea, in a river.

examples.text: There's no-one **in the room** / **in the building** / **in the garden**.
What do you have **in your hand** / **in your mouth**?
When we were **in Italy**, we spent a few days **in Venice**.
I have a friend who lives **in a small village in the mountains**.
There were some people swimming **in the pool** / **in the sea** / **in the river**.

lesson.heading: at = a point or a place
lesson.text: We use **at** when we think of a place as a point: at the bus stop, at the door, at the roundabout, at her desk. We also use **at** for the place where we get on or off something.

examples.text: Who is that man standing **at the bus stop** / **at the door** / **at the window**?
Turn left **at the traffic lights** / **at the next junction** / **at the roundabout** / **at the church**.
We have to get off the bus **at the next stop**.
When you leave the hotel, please leave your key **at reception**.

left.label: in = inside the space
examples: There were a lot of people **in the shop**. It was crowded.
I'll meet you **in the hotel lobby**. (= in the building)

right.label: at = the point on the way
examples: Go along this road, then turn left **at the shop**.
I'll meet you **at the entrance** to the hotel. (= outside the building)

lesson.heading: on = on a surface
lesson.text: We use **on** for a surface or a line: on the wall, on the floor, on the ceiling, on a page, on an island.

examples.text: I sat **on the floor** / **on the ground** / **on the grass** / **on the beach** / **on a chair**.
There's a dirty mark **on the ceiling** / **on your nose** / **on your shirt**.
Did you see the notice **on the wall** / **on the door**?
You'll find details of TV programmes **on page seven** of the newspaper.
The hotel is **on a small island** in the middle of a lake.

lesson.heading: in or on? at or on?

left.label: inside it
examples: There is some water **in the bottle**.
There is somebody **at the door**. Shall I go and see who it is?

right.label: on the surface of it
examples: There is a label **on the bottle**.
There is a notice **on the door**. It says 'Do not disturb'.

lesson.text: Ask yourself: am I talking about a space (in), a point (at) or a surface (on)? The same noun can take all three - water in the bottle, a label on the bottle, meet me at the bottle bank.

exercises.prompt: There was a long queue of people ___ the bus stop.
exercises.explanation: A bus stop is a point on a journey, so we say at the bus stop.
We swim inside the water, so: in the river (also in the sea, in the pool).

exercises.prompt: He was holding something ___, but I couldn't see what it was.
exercises.explanation: Things we hold are in the hand: What do you have in your hand?

exercises.prompt: Nicola was wearing a silver ring ___ her little finger.
exercises.explanation: A ring sits on the surface of the finger, so we say on her little finger.

exercises.prompt: Leave the motorway ___ and then turn left.
exercises.explanation: A junction is a point on the road: turn left at the next junction.

exercises.prompt: Match the beginning of each sentence with the right place phrase.

exercises.statement: There is some water on the bottle and there is a label in the bottle.
exercises.explanation: There is some water in the bottle and there is a label on the bottle. The water is inside, the label is on the surface.

exercises.prompt: You can go skiing ___. There's plenty of snow.
exercises.explanation: We say in the mountains, as with in a village, in the country.

exercises.prompt: Which preposition goes with each place?
I wouldn't like an office job. I couldn't spend the whole day sitting ___ a desk.
exercises.explanation: We sit at a desk, at a table, at the window - a point where we are.
We say on an island, as with on the beach and on the coast.

exercises.prompt: I like that picture hanging on the wall ___ the kitchen.
exercises.explanation: The kitchen is a room, so the picture is in the kitchen (and on the wall).
